name: Pens - Beers
description: Design graph for the 'Beers' screen of a hockey-team companion app ('Pens'), reconstructed from a single static screenshot. The screen reports season beer consumption for the team 'PENGUINS / DORVAL YOUNGTIMERS': a hero metric, a 52-cell case tracker with legend, a two-column grid of stat cards, and a five-item bottom tab bar with 'Beers' selected. No behaviour is asserted: the only source is an image, so the graph contains no triggers and no navigates-to edges.

sourceSummary.label: Single application-window screenshot, 470 x 945 px, dark theme, desktop window chrome visible.

metadata.unoMappingDiscipline: Every properties.uno object in this graph is a PROPOSED realization, never a declared fact: a raster image cannot reveal control types, x:Names, style keys, resource keys or class names. Each uno object therefore carries evidenceKind:"inferred" and no declared identifiers (no xName, styleKey, resourceKey or class appear anywhere in this graph).
metadata.behaviourDiscipline: Zero triggers and zero navigates-to edges were emitted. Visible affordances (tabs, tappable-looking cells) are recorded structurally only; their behaviour is deferred to unresolved.
metadata.measurementNote: Geometry, colours and radii were sampled from the raster. Solid fills are exact; text colours and corner radii are antialiased estimates and are marked with reduced confidence.

unresolved.question: What does activating each bottom tab do - which screen does each one show, and is the bar a navigation surface or a filter?
unresolved.reason: The only input is a static image. Labels such as 'Schedule' and 'Roster' suggest sibling screens, but no navigation destination is observable, so no navigates-to or triggers edges were emitted.

unresolved.question: Are the 52 tracker cells interactive (tap a cell to mark a case consumed) or a read-only readout?
unresolved.reason: Nothing in a still frame distinguishes a tappable cell from a painted one; the cell is therefore typed as a component with role 'indicator' rather than as a control.

unresolved.question: Should consumed/remaining be two states of one cell, or two design-system variants of a cell component?
unresolved.reason: Modelled as states because the distinction is data-driven (how many cases have been drunk) rather than an authored design choice, but the legend presents them as two named categories, which reads as variants.

unresolved.question: What content sits below the second row of stat cards?
unresolved.reason: The scrollbar thumb covers roughly 82% of its track and the lower stat cards are clipped square at the viewport edge, so a further band of content exists that this frame does not show. The stats region may hold more than four cards.

unresolved.question: What do the empty, loading and error presentations of this screen look like?
unresolved.reason: Only one populated frame was supplied. No screen-level state nodes were emitted rather than invent conditions that were never observed.

unresolved.question: Is '780 beers' computed from the case count (26 cases x 30 per case = 780) or an independently sourced figure?
unresolved.reason: The arithmetic is consistent, but asserting the derivation would be inventing a business rule from a coincidence of three visible numbers.

unresolved.question: Is the top strip an app-extended custom title bar or default OS window chrome?
unresolved.reason: The strip renders in a grey distinct from the app palette and carries standard caption buttons, which points to system chrome, but a themed custom title bar would look the same. The caption buttons were not modelled as nodes for the same reason.

unresolved.question: What is the exact foreground colour of the '26 / 52 cases' progress counter?
unresolved.reason: Its brightest sample (~#BDE2F4) is a pale blue measurably cooler than the pure white of the team name, but the glyphs are small and heavily antialiased. It was left untokenised rather than folded into either the primary or the secondary text token.

unresolved.question: Which font families, weights, sizes and letter-spacing values does this screen use?
unresolved.reason: A raster cannot identify a family. The three typography tokens record observable treatment (condensed heavy display, tracked-out uppercase label, regular-width mixed-case body) without naming a family, and the split between the label and body faces rests on casing and width alone - they may be one family at two settings.

unresolved.question: What are the exact corner radii, paddings and gutters?
unresolved.reason: All four values were measured from antialiased pixel edges. Card corners bracket roughly 8-14 px and are assumed to be one shared value; page padding measures 21-24 px; card gutters measure 9-12 px.

unresolved.question: Do the season-tracker card and the stat cards realize one shared card component?
unresolved.reason: They share an exact surface colour and an apparently shared radius, but differ in size, padding, internal structure and count, so they were modelled as separate concepts that both consume the surface and radius tokens rather than consolidated behind one canonical.

unresolved.question: Why is the Beers tab icon a full-colour pictograph while the other four are monochrome stroke glyphs?
possibleValues: the selected state swaps in a colour icon
the Beers tab always uses a colour icon regardless of selection
the icon set is simply mixed
unresolved.reason: Only one selection state is visible, so the colour icon cannot be attributed to selection versus to that item's identity.

unresolved.question: Is the team logo, name and subtitle fixed branding or data that varies per team?
unresolved.reason: The header reads as team identity that a multi-team app would bind, but a single frame cannot distinguish bound data from a hard-coded brand.
